subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should oversized workspace ignore files use the proposed 4 MiB terminal fail-closed policy, even though this makes the entire affected subtree disappear from skill and workspace discovery for existing users?
rationale: The code can enforce several internally consistent policies, but choosing between preserving visibility and conservatively enforcing an unreadable exclusion policy changes both the security boundary and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Approve Terminal Fail-Closed
options.body: Accept the 4 MiB cap and whole-subtree exclusion as the secure default, then land after exact-head checks pass.

options.title: Require Visible Recovery Guidance
options.body: Keep terminal fail-closed behavior but add a clear runtime diagnostic naming the oversized policy file, cap, and recovery action before merge.

options.title: Preserve Fail-Open Compatibility
options.body: Bound and skip oversized policy files with a warning, preserving discovery at the cost of potentially scanning content the user intended to exclude.

recommendation.title: Approve Terminal Fail-Closed
recommendation.body: Accept the 4 MiB cap and whole-subtree exclusion as the secure default, then land after exact-head checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent grouped-discovery and symlink-policy commits make them the strongest available owner for this security-versus-compatibility choice.
